insights.concise_text: TCEN addresses the common pre-training practice's subnet waste, role mismatch and non-pre-trained attention issues by reusing all subnets, keeping roles consistent, and pre-training the attention module.

triple.subject: TCEN
triple.object: subnet waste, role mismatch and non-pre-trained attention issues

insights.concise_text: Because the common practice initializes ST with only the ASR encoder and MT decoder, the MT encoder's valuable semantic information cannot be inherited by the final ST system.

triple.subject: common practice
triple.object: loss of valuable semantic information captured by the MT encoder

insights.concise_text: TCEN's tandem ASR encoder and MT encoder disentangle acoustic and linguistic feature extraction, addressing the role mismatch caused by the speech encoder's changing roles.

triple.subject: TCEN's tandem ASR encoder and MT encoder
triple.object: role mismatch

insights.concise_text: TCEN reuses the pre-trained MT attention module in ST, overcoming the prior limitation that the ST attention module did not benefit from pre-training.

triple.subject: TCEN
triple.object: non-pre-trained attention module

insights.concise_text: The TCEN text encoder receives word embeddings in MT but speech encoder outputs in ST, so sharing the CTC projection matrix with the word embedding matrix targets semantic consistency.

triple.subject: sharing the CTC projection matrix with the word embedding matrix
triple.object: semantic inconsistency between MT and ST inputs

insights.concise_text: Because speech encoder output length is proportional to input frame length and much longer than word embeddings, lengthening MT source sentences with repetitions and blank tokens targets length inconsistency.

triple.subject: lengthening MT source sentences with word repetitions and blank tokens
triple.object: length inconsistency

insights.concise_text: TCEN is evaluated on the IWSLT18 speech translation benchmark and is significantly better than previous methods by 3.6 and 2.2 BLEU scores for subword-level and character-level decoding.

triple.subject: TCEN
triple.object: IWSLT18 speech translation benchmark

insights.concise_text: The CTC-based ASR pre-training of enc_s on dataset A enables TCEN to avoid an ASR decoder while still reading acoustic features into the source language space.

triple.subject: CTC-based ASR pre-training of enc_s on dataset A
triple.object: TCEN without an ASR decoder

insights.concise_text: TCEN's pre-training uses CTC objective for enc_s on dataset A and MT dataset M for enc_t and dec, then fine-tuning jointly updates ASR, MT, and ST tasks.

triple.subject: TCEN training procedure
triple.object: CTC pre-training on dataset A, MT pre-training on dataset M, and joint ASR, MT, and ST fine-tuning

insights.concise_text: The many-to-many multi-task model's task-specific attention explains why previous work trains separate ASR, MT and ST attention modules and leaves ST attention unbenefited by pre-training.

triple.subject: task-specific attention
triple.object: ST attention not benefiting from pre-training

insights.concise_text: TCEN is evaluated on IWSLT18 speech translation task using lowercase BLEU, with tst2010, tst2013, tst2014, tst2015 as test sets.

triple.subject: TCEN
triple.object: IWSLT18 speech translation task with lowercase BLEU on tst2010, tst2013, tst2014, tst2015

insights.concise_text: The ASR model used for encoder pre-training is trained on ST-TED and TED-LIUM2, which together provide 272 hours and 207 hours of English speech.

triple.subject: ASR model used for encoder pre-training
triple.object: ST-TED and TED-LIUM2 with 272 hours and 207 hours of English speech

insights.concise_text: The MT model used for decoder pre-training is first trained on WMT data, corresponding to WMT2018 out-of-domain training data with 41M sentence pairs.

triple.subject: MT model used for decoder pre-training
triple.object: WMT2018 out-of-domain training data with 41M sentence pairs

insights.concise_text: The MT model used for decoder pre-training is fine-tuned on in-domain data consisting of ST-TED and WIT3 transcription and translation pairs with 130k and 200k sentence pairs.

triple.subject: MT model used for decoder pre-training
triple.object: ST-TED and WIT3 in-domain MT data with 130k and 200k sentence pairs

insights.concise_text: The claim that the MT dataset is much larger than the ASR dataset is supported by WMT2018 having 41M sentence pairs versus TED-LIUM2 having 93k transcript sentences.

triple.subject: WMT2018 with 41M sentence pairs
triple.object: the MT dataset being much larger than the ASR dataset

insights.concise_text: The vanilla model starts at low accuracy because it is trained from scratch on ST-TED and its networks are not pre-trained on ASR and MT data.

triple.subject: training from scratch on ST-TED without ASR and MT pre-training
triple.object: the vanilla model to start at low accuracy

insights.concise_text: The proposed method reuses every sub-net and keeps sub-net roles consistent, and empirical studies demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms baselines.

triple.subject: reusing every sub-net and keeping sub-net roles consistent
triple.object: baselines in empirical studies

insights.concise_text: The char-level models outperform subword-level models in all settings, while subword experiments use English and German vocabularies generated by sentencepiece with 5k tokens.

triple.subject: sentencepiece 5k-token subword vocabularies
triple.object: subword-level models that char-level models outperform in all settings

insights.concise_text: The ablation study on subword-level experiments uses the setting where English and German vocabularies are generated by sentencepiece with a fixed size of 5k tokens.

triple.subject: ablation study on subword-level experiments
triple.object: sentencepiece English and German vocabularies with a fixed size of 5k tokens

insights.concise_text: The end-to-end model compared with cascaded systems is TCEN, implemented based on ESPnet with RNN size d=1024 for all models.

triple.subject: TCEN
triple.object: ESPnet and RNN size d=1024 in the cascaded-system comparison
